Then there's trademarks (branding.) I was talking this with one of the better lawyers in the field - the annual cost for trademark coverage in the Western world starts at about $1 million US - each and every year. That does not protect your brand outside of the West.

So there is the building up the business locally - and having a website that covers local sales and deliveries, etc. For regional stuff it is usually better to wholesale the brand through a bigger distribution outfit that has all of the border related stuff already in place, and also has the network of retailers already set up. This way you can focus on your product without dealing with mountains of paperwork and regulatory burden.

If you go national, you are almost always going through one of the established major players - they are full able to jump all of the hurdles concerning regulations etc, and will take over the branding and distribution (and sometimes production) of your product.
